focuses.title: A New Reform Mandate
focuses.description: The election has given Reform the largest delegation in the Riigikogu. Agree a programme with the parties that actually support our cabinet, placing defence, public finances and public services before the new parliament. This programme belongs to the elected government and can continue under its designated successor.

focuses.title: Three Percent for National Defence
focuses.description: Adopt the government's three-percent defence-spending commitment and fund the first procurement instalments. Give the Defence Forces a dependable planning horizon instead of announcing capabilities without money. The higher spending is a continuing obligation on Estonia's small economy.

focuses.title: Equip a 20,000-Strong Territorial Defence
focuses.description: Support the expanded territorial-defence structure through instructors, stores and reserve appointments. Kaitseliit units need reliable equipment accounting and rehearsed reporting arrangements. Fund organisation and training within existing recruitment and production; a paper establishment does not supply twenty thousand new soldiers.

focuses.title: Procure Layered Air Defence
focuses.description: Advance the medium-range air-defence procurement undertaken with Latvia, alongside short-range protection, radar links and trained crews. Coordinate contracts with partners able to supply them in this timeline. Procurement preparation improves the army's resilience without conjuring a battery or bypassing equipment production.

focuses.title: Prepare the Baltic Defence Line
focuses.description: Survey defensive positions and storage sites with the other Baltic states. Arrange land agreements and stockpile obstacles and construction material for a dispersed defensive line. These works strengthen planned positions; they do not make Estonia's entire border an impassable wall.

focuses.title: Expand Nursipalu and Compensate Residents
focuses.description: Carry out the decision to enlarge the Nursipalu training area. Finance exercises and facilities for Estonian and allied units while paying fair compensation and supporting affected municipalities. More demanding training should be accompanied by a credible agreement with the people who live beside it.

focuses.title: Stock the Reception Areas for Allied Forces
focuses.description: Prepare reception areas, transport schedules and dispersed stores for allied reinforcements. Coordinate ammunition compatibility and host-nation support with the partners available to Estonia. This improves our ability to sustain operations without duplicating allied divisions supplied by TFR's existing reinforcement decisions.

focuses.title: Plan a Defence Industrial Park
focuses.description: Use the national special-planning procedure to identify sites for ammunition, explosives and defence technology. Resolve access, utilities, safety distances and environmental assessment before promising production. The state prepares the site; firms still need contracts, workers and equipment.

focuses.title: Finance an Ammunition Production Line
focuses.description: Finance one first-stage ammunition workshop on a serviced defence-industry site. Pair the investment with procurement commitments and inspection capacity. This is an accelerated TFR adaptation of the industrial-park programme, not a claim that the historical park opened in thirty-five days.

focuses.title: Contract Domestic Drone and Repair Workshops
focuses.description: Place defence-industry orders for drone assembly, inspection and field repairs. Give domestic suppliers a second funded production facility while keeping designs and deliveries subject to ordinary procurement. The investment adds production capacity rather than free aircraft, ammunition or divisions.

focuses.title: Complete the Grid's European Connection Works
focuses.description: Fund the remaining connection and control-system works needed for a secure European electricity system. The Baltic transmission operators have already undertaken extensive preparations. Finish the practical work and strengthen reserve arrangements without assuming that every neighbouring country has followed its historical path.

focuses.title: Clear the Wind-Power Permit Backlog
focuses.description: Resource municipal planning teams and simplify the permit stages that delay viable wind developments. Keep the environmental assessment and local consultation that projects require. Faster decisions and stronger networks can attract new generation without declaring every proposed wind farm complete.

focuses.title: Open the Regional Apartment-Renovation Round
focuses.description: Continue the large apartment-building renovation programme with regional allocations. Help associations prepare technically sound insulation, heating and ventilation projects, including outside the largest cities. Lower energy demand and dependable construction contracts strengthen households and local businesses together.

focuses.title: Fund the Transition to Estonian Education
focuses.description: Prepare kindergartens and the first and fourth grades for the transition to Estonian-language instruction. Fund materials, language support and school-level implementation. Starting the transition is a practical programme; the full school system cannot be transformed in a single term of office.

focuses.title: Recruit Teachers for Ida-Viru Schools
focuses.description: Use additional pay, mentoring and teacher training to fill posts in Ida-Viru County. Schools need qualified staff who can teach their subject in Estonian and help pupils learn it. Direct resources toward the shortage instead of treating a change of classroom language as a completed staffing plan.

focuses.title: Negotiate Teachers' Pay and Career Progression
focuses.description: Negotiate with teachers and school owners on pay, workload and a clear career framework. Back the settlement with funding and transparent responsibilities. The real negotiations involved disputes and limited resources; an agreement must be affordable as well as attractive to the next generation of teachers.

focuses.title: Keep Young People Learning Until Eighteen
focuses.description: Replace the school-attendance obligation with a broader obligation to learn until eighteen. Prepare flexible general and vocational routes, guidance and municipal follow-up. The purpose is to prevent pupils leaving basic school without a useful next step, rather than merely extending time spent in a classroom.

focuses.title: Align Vocational Places with Employer Demand
focuses.description: Rework vocational admissions and practical courses with employers and schools. Expand places where Estonia lacks technical skills and strengthen routes into further study. Better preparation helps workshops and public services recruit qualified people without granting the state an unlimited labour reserve.

focuses.title: Build Metrosert's Applied-Research Capacity
focuses.description: Equip Metrosert's new applied-research unit and connect its specialists with Estonian firms. Support testing and development in fields such as drones, autonomous systems and health data. The centre closes practical gaps between a promising design and a product that a company can make reliably.

focuses.title: Replace Repeated Reports with Data Exchange
focuses.description: Implement the real-time-economy programme through common data standards and automatic reporting. Firms should send accurate information once and know how the state uses it. Begin with workable reporting flows and reliable registers instead of replacing every form with another disconnected portal.

focuses.title: Take Firms Through the Digitalisation Masterclass
focuses.description: Support businesses in mapping production bottlenecks and adopting useful digital systems. The enterprise programme should combine training with a practical investment plan, especially for smaller firms. Productivity gains come from changes on the shop floor and in administration, not from purchasing software alone.

focuses.title: Organise the Digital Defence Reserve
focuses.description: Connect Defence Forces and Kaitseliit specialists with the operators of essential public systems. Rehearse restoration from backups and a common response to hostile information operations. Estonia's electronic services must remain useful when ordinary communications and institutions come under pressure.

focuses.title: Protect One Percent for Public Research
focuses.description: Keep public research and development funding at the government's one-percent-of-GDP commitment and encourage private investment alongside it. Publish priorities and review results while preserving stable support for research institutions. Fiscal consolidation should not leave essential technical work without a planning horizon.

focuses.title: Back Regional Exporters and Investment Projects
focuses.description: Use enterprise support and economic diplomacy to help firms outside the largest cities reach new customers. Assess projects for viable products, skilled jobs and access to services. Regional investment should complement private decisions rather than preserve every uneconomic business indefinitely.

focuses.title: Fund the Civil-Protection Reserve
focuses.description: Train a community-based reserve to support rescue and health services during serious emergencies. Municipalities need agreed responsibilities, communications and supplies for evacuation and shelter. Civil preparation helps the country endure the opening of a European war without turning volunteers into unprovided army formations.

focuses.title: Raise VAT to Twenty-Two Percent
focuses.description: Legislate the increase in the standard VAT rate from twenty to twenty-two percent and fund the Tax and Customs Board's implementation. Additional receipts help finance defence and public services, while the higher consumption tax imposes a real cost on households. Account for both sides of the measure.

focuses.title: Review Ministry Spending Before New Commitments
focuses.description: Review recurrent spending and procurement across ministries, distinguishing avoidable overhead from services that still need funding. Publish the savings and their consequences. A spending review provides fiscal room only where government actually changes how money is used.

focuses.title: Strengthen the Municipal Revenue Base
focuses.description: Rebalance municipal revenue so that local services do not depend entirely on the number of high earners living nearby. Coordinate the transition with councils and publish the distribution. Small municipalities need a dependable basis for schools, care and crisis duties.

focuses.title: Put Municipal Funding Behind Care Reform
focuses.description: Implement the care reform with local authorities paying the care component of general residential care. Inspect staffing, fees and access so that families see the support in practice. Continue a reform legislated before this cabinet and bring its administration into the new government's programme.

focuses.title: Enact Marriage Equality
focuses.description: Amend the Family Law Act so that two adults may marry and provide the implementing rules that registrars and families require. The law replaces the earlier referendum dispute with a parliamentary settlement. Publish clear arrangements for existing partnerships and equal treatment before the law.

focuses.title: Keep Mental-Health Support Close to Home
focuses.description: Continue grants for municipal counselling and psychologists in primary care. Link local help with specialist treatment and review whether residents can actually obtain an appointment. Accessible support matters to daily life and becomes more valuable when families face mobilisation, displacement or bereavement.

focuses.title: Report to the Riigikogu on the Mandate
focuses.description: Present the completed government's programme to parliament: the tax choices, schools and services funded, energy security improved and defence preparations delivered. Review what remains unfinished beyond these initial projects. This report neither starts a war nor calls an election; the postwar parliament will judge the cabinet when independent politics can resume.

focuses.title: An EKRE-Led Parliamentary Mandate
focuses.description: EKRE has won the largest delegation. Negotiate a funded programme with our actual coalition partners; a plurality still needs a parliamentary majority.

focuses.title: Fund the Three-Percent Defence Commitment
focuses.description: Approve procurement instalments and command preparations before a European war reaches Estonia. A spending commitment must be matched by contracts and dependable stores.

focuses.title: Prepare the Expanded Reserve Establishment
focuses.description: Schedule instructors, call-up records and equipment accounting for a larger reserve. Expansion remains a training and procurement task rather than an instant addition to the army.

focuses.title: Finance Air Defence for Key Regions
focuses.description: Fund site planning, crews and procurement for medium- and short-range protection. Integrate the systems we can maintain instead of promising an immediate nationwide shield.

focuses.title: Prepare Coastal Positions and Mine Stores
focuses.description: Prepare shore positions, observation posts and controlled stores for coastal defence. Naval and ground commanders must agree responsibilities before hostilities begin.

focuses.title: Organise a Military Border-Guard Reserve
focuses.description: Define the proposed border service's crisis command and reserve duties. Train personnel and finance communications without treating an administrative change as a new field army.

focuses.title: Fund Shelters and Civil-Protection Training
focuses.description: Survey shelters, fund essential repairs and require protection in major new buildings. Municipal exercises should test evacuation, first aid and continuity of services.

focuses.title: Place Maintainable Domestic Defence Contracts
focuses.description: Translate equipment plans into contracts that Estonian suppliers can service. Start with ammunition handling and repairs while preserving ordinary production and procurement limits.

focuses.title: Finance an Ammunition Workshop
focuses.description: Pay for one inspected ammunition-production workshop. This initial facility supplies Estonia's production base; it does not deliver an automatic stockpile or complete the entire rearmament programme.

focuses.title: Finance an Equipment Repair Workshop
focuses.description: Fund a second workshop for servicing, component manufacture and overhaul. Reliable maintenance keeps procured equipment useful; Estonia must still manufacture or purchase the equipment itself.

focuses.title: Redirect Investment to Existing Railways
focuses.description: Review Rail Baltic commitments and redirect this programme's investment toward existing railway links. Publish the contractual costs and prioritize usable domestic connections.

focuses.title: Fund the Tallinn Trunk-Road Sections
focuses.description: Select and fund practical four-lane sections toward Tartu, Pärnu and Narva. Phased construction improves movement without declaring three complete highways finished at once.

focuses.title: Contract Domestic Emergency Food Reserves
focuses.description: Contract inspected staple-food reserves and rotate them through domestic suppliers. Farmers and transport operators need payment and clear emergency delivery arrangements.

focuses.title: Overhaul the Idle Narva Power Blocks
focuses.description: Commission technical surveys and overhaul contracts for idle generating units. Fund dependable capacity and fuel arrangements while accounting for operating and environmental costs.

focuses.title: Bring Kiisa Capacity into the Supply Plan
focuses.description: Review the gas station's company structure and commercial availability. Secure fuel and dispatch arrangements while keeping emergency reserve requirements explicit.

focuses.title: Fund the Three-Cent Electricity Proposal
focuses.description: Prepare the proposed state-backed supply contracts and their subsidy reserve. Resolve carbon-cost and legal disputes; a promised tariff does not make electricity generation free.

focuses.title: Lower Fuel Excise to the EU Minimum
focuses.description: Reduce the proposed fuel duties and update tax administration. Lower operating costs help firms and households, while the treasury loses recurring receipts.

focuses.title: Introduce Five-Percent VAT on Food
focuses.description: Legislate the reduced food rate and monitor how the change reaches customers. Record the revenue loss alongside the relief delivered to household budgets.

focuses.title: Reduce Medicine VAT to Five Percent
focuses.description: Apply the proposed lower rate to medicines and update pharmacy billing. Improved affordability requires a funded revenue adjustment and continued access to supplies.

focuses.title: Link Parents' Tax Relief to Children
focuses.description: Draft the child-linked income-tax allowance with clear eligibility and legal limits. Publish its distribution and recurring cost before claiming the policy pays for itself.

focuses.title: Pilot Child-Linked Family Home Loans
focuses.description: Fund a limited loan programme with child-linked repayment relief. Begin with assessed borrowers and a defined public guarantee rather than underwriting every mortgage.

focuses.title: Fund Parents' Student-Loan Relief
focuses.description: Create an application process for the proposed child-linked student-loan cancellation. Budget the first claims and explain the eligibility rules to lenders and families.

focuses.title: Finance Duty Hours for Family Doctors
focuses.description: Contract additional primary-care duty hours and local pharmacy cover. Patients need reliable appointments and referrals rather than another promise of shorter queues.

focuses.title: Restore Round-the-Clock Midwife Cover
focuses.description: Fund midwife duty arrangements in smaller hospitals and family practices. Assess staffing and safe referral routes before extending the service.

focuses.title: Budget the Thirteenth-Pension Supplement
focuses.description: Fund the proposed additional annual payment for pensioners below the average pension. Explain who receives it and provide for the cost alongside defence spending.

focuses.title: Strengthen Parliamentary Security Scrutiny
focuses.description: Fund committee expertise and lawful access to oversight information. Review institutional accountability while maintaining operational secrecy and independent proceedings.

focuses.title: Commission an Independent E-Voting Audit
focuses.description: Commission independent technical scrutiny and publish the findings. The audit does not presume fraud, change allocated seats or call another election.

focuses.title: Draft the Citizens' Initiative Procedure
focuses.description: Prepare the proposed procedure for citizen-initiated bills and referendums. Establish signature verification and constitutional safeguards before seeking the necessary parliamentary approval.

focuses.title: Draft Direct Presidential Elections
focuses.description: Prepare the constitutional amendment and its required procedure. Introducing a bill does not replace the incumbent president or bypass the existing constitution.

focuses.title: Review European Measures in the Riigikogu
focuses.description: Resource constitutional scrutiny of proposed European measures and the government's negotiating mandate. Publish disputed obligations without automatically withdrawing Estonia from its alliances.

focuses.title: Fund Estonian-Language Teaching Capacity
focuses.description: Prepare teachers and teaching materials for Estonian-language instruction. Budget practical support for pupils and institutions instead of treating a legislative requirement as sufficient staffing.

focuses.title: Account for the National Conservative Programme
focuses.description: Report the programme's costs and results to the Riigikogu. Review incomplete legislation and long projects without calling an election or changing the European war's course.

focuses.title: A New Centre-Led Mandate
focuses.description: Centre has won the largest delegation. Jüri Ratas must agree a funded programme with the actual coalition, linking public services and regional investment to defence preparation.

focuses.title: Fund the Cross-Party Defence Commitment
focuses.description: Invite parliamentary parties to a common defence agreement and fund its first procurement instalments. Publish lifetime costs so a spending pledge supports usable capabilities.

focuses.title: Finance Medium-Range Air Defence Preparation
focuses.description: Budget sites, crews and joint procurement planning with available allies. An integrated protection plan must account for maintenance and deliveries before declaring a new capability.

focuses.title: Put Reservists' Civilian Skills to Work
focuses.description: Match reserve appointments to civilian expertise and fund refresher instruction. Engineers, medics and transport specialists need reliable records and ordinary recruitment arrangements.

focuses.title: Prepare Permanent Allied Reception Facilities
focuses.description: Finance reception, communications and dispersed stores for allied troops. Existing reinforcement decisions remain separate; new facilities improve how Estonia sustains the forces that actually arrive.

focuses.title: Agree Training-Area Compensation with Communities
focuses.description: Negotiate access, compensation and exercise arrangements with councils and residents. Defence training needs usable land and instructors alongside a settlement people can understand.

focuses.title: Rehearse Municipal Civil Protection
focuses.description: Fund municipal warning, evacuation and essential-service exercises. Coordinate councils, employers and rescue services so civilian preparation supports the army's ability to keep operating.

focuses.title: Back Domestic Defence Suppliers
focuses.description: Set aside guarantees and development funding for maintainable domestic contracts. Give suppliers clear inspection and delivery requirements instead of replacing procurement with announcements.

focuses.title: Finance a Domestic Ammunition Workshop
focuses.description: Fund one inspected production workshop and the supplier contracts needed to operate it. The project adds capacity; ammunition must still enter through ordinary production or paid procurement.

focuses.title: Finance an Equipment Maintenance Workshop
focuses.description: Pay for a second facility able to overhaul equipment and make replacement components. Domestic maintenance keeps purchases useful without awarding free vehicles or another army.

focuses.title: Fund New Technology in Ida-Viru Industry
focuses.description: Select viable modernization projects with local employers and research institutions. Innovation funding should support productive jobs as the county's industrial base changes.

focuses.title: Guarantee Investment in High-Unemployment Regions
focuses.description: Offer assessed investment guarantees and retraining in regions with fewer jobs. Publish outcomes and risks so regional policy creates opportunities rather than concealing failing projects.

focuses.title: Place the Funded Public Construction Orders
focuses.description: Tender a staged public-building programme and disclose its financing. Predictable orders can sustain construction skills while delivering facilities that municipalities actually need.

focuses.title: Keep Dispatchable Generation and LNG Options Ready
focuses.description: Fund reliable generating reserves and permanent-terminal preparation. Keep existing capacity usable while alternative supplies develop, with fuel and operating costs included.

focuses.title: Support Local Heat-and-Power Projects
focuses.description: Finance viable combined heat-and-power projects and their network access. Local heat demand and sustainable fuel contracts should determine which schemes receive support.

focuses.title: Lower the Rural Renovation Contribution
focuses.description: Fund apartment renovations outside the largest cities with a smaller local contribution. Technical supervision and affordable loans help associations deliver lasting energy savings.

focuses.title: Weatherproof the Distribution Grid
focuses.description: Prioritize vulnerable lines and connection bottlenecks with transmission and distribution operators. Underground works and stronger substations need agreed sites, budgets and maintenance.

focuses.title: Finish Affordable Last-Mile Connections
focuses.description: Support household and enterprise connections where commercial rollout remains insufficient. Coordinate trenches and public works to reduce disruption and reach isolated settlements.

focuses.title: Finance Community Energy Cooperatives
focuses.description: Offer assessed financing and technical advice for local generation and storage. Communities need viable projects and transparent ownership rather than a promise of unlimited cheap power.

focuses.title: Introduce the Thirty-Percent Upper Income Band
focuses.description: Legislate the higher band for income above twice the average wage and prepare tax administration. Budget additional receipts while accounting for opposition to the distributional change.

focuses.title: Link the Tax Allowance to the Minimum Wage
focuses.description: Apply the proposed minimum-wage exemption with clear payroll guidance. Lower earners retain more income, while the treasury records the recurring cost alongside the new upper band.

focuses.title: Reduce Food VAT to Five Percent
focuses.description: Legislate the reduced food rate and check how retailers pass it through. Finance the revenue loss explicitly rather than assuming lower prices eliminate the budget tradeoff.

focuses.title: Remove VAT from Prescription Medicines
focuses.description: Prepare the proposed exemption and lower rate for other medicines. Update pharmacy billing and monitor access while recording the reduction in public receipts.

focuses.title: Fund the Next Fifty-Euro Pension Step
focuses.description: Finance the first extraordinary increase in the basic pension component. It is a funded step toward the party's longer-term pension objective, rather than an instant fulfilment of every future payment.

focuses.title: Expand Municipal Home Nursing and Care
focuses.description: Contract more care at home with councils and health providers. Dependable visits and support for family carers can preserve independence and reduce pressure on institutional services.

focuses.title: Give County Hospitals Predictable Budgets
focuses.description: Fund county hospitals against assessed service needs, including areas with fewer patients. A dependable budget should preserve access while requiring reporting on staffing and treatment.

focuses.title: Restore Sick Pay from the Second Day
focuses.description: Fund the proposed shared compensation arrangement with employers. Employees gain a clearer basis for staying home when ill, and the public contribution remains visible.

focuses.title: Compensate Councils for Free Kindergarten Places
focuses.description: Finance the municipal cost of the promised places and review capacity. Fee relief must be accompanied by staff and premises so parents can actually use the service.

focuses.title: Negotiate the Teachers' Pay Roadmap
focuses.description: Agree funded pay steps with municipalities and unions. Staffing and support specialists must be included alongside the longer-term salary objective.

focuses.title: Offer Free Estonian Courses and Study Leave
focuses.description: Finance language instruction adapted to work and daily life, including support for citizenship applicants. Clear access and paid learning time help residents participate in public institutions.

focuses.title: Convene the National-Minorities Advisory Council
focuses.description: Create a consultative forum and support community cultural organizations. Publish its recommendations and connect them with practical public-service access without changing electoral eligibility.

focuses.title: Report on the Centre Government's Programme
focuses.description: Present the investment, tax and service accounts to the Riigikogu. Assess defence readiness and the projects still in progress without calling an election or directing the European war.

focuses.title: Fund the Independent Defence Establishment
focuses.description: Authorize the next procurement instalments and publish a funded readiness plan. Estonia's defence commitments require contracts, instructors and dependable stores.

focuses.title: Prepare Integrated Air Defence Sites
focuses.description: Fund crew instruction, communications and assessed procurement sites. This capability programme must account for operating costs before equipment can be fielded.

focuses.title: Rehearse the Reserve Mobilisation System
focuses.description: Check call-up records, employers' arrangements and unit stores through scheduled exercises. A reliable muster makes existing formations more usable when warning time is short.

focuses.title: Build Kaitseliit Training and Range Capacity
focuses.description: Finance instructors and safe range access with local agreements. Territorial units need frequent practice and practical facilities to improve their small-unit work.

focuses.title: Prepare Allied Reception and Prepositioned Stores
focuses.description: Tender reception facilities and dispersed storage with the allies available to Estonia. Exercise their use; the ordinary allied reinforcement arrangements still govern troop arrivals.

focuses.title: Give Civil Protection a Funded Legal Basis
focuses.description: Agree responsibilities for warning, evacuation and essential supplies. Councils and rescue services receive exercise funding and clear reporting duties.

focuses.title: Back Defence-Industry Development Contracts
focuses.description: Fund inspected prototypes and supply contracts with domestic firms. Publish the delivery standards so public development money supports production that the armed forces can maintain.

focuses.title: Finance an Ammunition Production Workshop
focuses.description: Pay for a limited production facility and its supplier qualification. The workshop adds industrial capacity; completed ammunition still comes through normal production or paid procurement.

focuses.title: Finance an Equipment Maintenance Workshop
focuses.description: Fund a second facility for overhaul work and replacement components. Sustainable servicing turns purchases into a usable force without awarding free equipment.

focuses.title: Finance Regional Manufacturing Partnerships
focuses.description: Co-fund viable supplier projects with county development centres and researchers. Regional firms should gain skills, orders and access to higher-value work.

focuses.title: Establish a Positive Credit Register
focuses.description: Set consistent reporting and data-access rules for a responsible lending register. Better assessment should help sound borrowers obtain competing offers while preserving personal-data controls.

focuses.title: Update the Fixed Business-Expense Allowances
focuses.description: Legislate revised travel and work-expense exemptions with clear payroll instructions. Record the revenue reduction alongside simpler administration for employers.

focuses.title: Contract Dispatchable Domestic Power Reserves
focuses.description: Fund available generating reserves and their fuel arrangements. Reliability contracts must cover maintenance and dispatch obligations while new supply is developed.

focuses.title: Finance Secure Grid Connections
focuses.description: Pay for assessed connection bottlenecks and network works with system operators. Agree technical tests before depending on an additional source of supply.

focuses.title: Standardise and Fund Energy-Saving Renovation
focuses.description: Give housing associations funded designs, technical supervision and predictable applications. Completed works reduce exposure to high energy bills over time.

focuses.title: Modernise District-Heating Networks
focuses.description: Tender viable pipe replacement and heating connections with municipalities. Review heat demand and maintenance before committing to each project.

focuses.title: Commission the Nuclear Feasibility and Safety Studies
focuses.description: Finance independent technical, regulatory and waste-management assessments. Parliament receives the evidence for a later investment decision; a study does not deliver a power station.

focuses.title: Fund the Extended Electricity Universal Service
focuses.description: Budget a defined support tranche for eligible households and smaller consumers. Publish the contract terms and review the public liability as market conditions change.

focuses.title: Legislate the Five-Thousand-Euro Child Allowance
focuses.description: Prepare the proposed annual child-linked income exemption and payroll guidance. Household relief has a recurring public revenue cost that must be recorded.

focuses.title: Permit Joint Income-Tax Returns for Spouses
focuses.description: Update tax administration and the rules for joint declarations. Explain eligibility and the resulting public cost before the first filing period.

focuses.title: Fund Equal Hundred-Euro Child Benefits
focuses.description: Finance the proposed first- and second-child benefit level with an administrative rollout. Review delivery with social-insurance officials and municipalities.

focuses.title: Launch the Large-Family Housing Grant Round
focuses.description: Open an assessed grant round for eligible large families and rural housing. Public guarantees and grants require realistic valuations and construction supervision.

focuses.title: Protect Care Benefits after Parental Leave
focuses.description: Fund revised care-benefit calculations for parents returning to work. Clear employer guidance helps families respond when a child falls ill.

focuses.title: Raise Child Maintenance Assistance to Two Hundred Euros
focuses.description: Finance the proposed assistance ceiling and strengthen recovery from liable parents. Coordinate claims so children receive support without unnecessary administrative delay.

focuses.title: Resource the Estonian-Language School Transition
focuses.description: Contract teacher training, learning materials and school support. A funded transition needs qualified staff and practical help for pupils in each municipality.

focuses.title: Fund Steps toward the Teachers' Pay Objective
focuses.description: Negotiate funded salary steps and training places with school owners. Publish progress toward the proposed minimum rather than declaring every staffing problem solved.

focuses.title: Agree the Public-Private Research Funding Compact
focuses.description: Award assessed research and industrial collaboration grants. Match public funding with credible private commitments and publish the results.

focuses.title: Fund Reliable Rural Broadband Connections
focuses.description: Target unserved connections with transparent tenders and shared civil works. Schools, firms and remote workers need a service that remains dependable in poor weather.

focuses.title: Guarantee Core Digital-Service Maintenance Funding
focuses.description: Budget security updates, continuity exercises and simpler data submission. Agencies must maintain the services already in use alongside new development.

focuses.title: Expand Financed Home-Care Services
focuses.description: Contract visits and support with councils and care providers. Review access and staffing so families can rely on practical help at home.

focuses.title: Present the Isamaa Government's Accounts
focuses.description: Report the funded programme and remaining obligations to the Riigikogu. Parliament should be able to assess defence preparation and service delivery before the next mandate.

focuses.title: A Social Democratic Parliamentary Mandate
focuses.description: SDE has won the largest delegation. Lauri Läänemets must assemble a majority capable of funding social protection alongside credible national defence.

focuses.title: Finance the Critical Defence Capabilities
focuses.description: Approve a funded procurement tranche and operating provision. Parliament will review deliveries and the next spending round before making further commitments.

focuses.title: Prepare Layered Air-Defence Procurement
focuses.description: Assess sites, train crews and contract compatible communications. The armed forces receive preparation for purchases that still require equipment and sustained funding.

focuses.title: Reorganise Rapid Reserve Mobilisation
focuses.description: Audit call-up assignments with employers and commanders. Exercises will test whether the existing reserve structure can assemble and sustain its units in time.

focuses.title: Resource Kaitseliit Instructors and Volunteers
focuses.description: Commission additional training sessions and inspected equipment maintenance. Volunteer defence needs predictable instruction and workable arrangements with civilian employment.

focuses.title: Prepare Reception Facilities for Allied Forces
focuses.description: Exercise reception routes and dispersed stores with Estonia's available allies. Normal reinforcement agreements still determine which allied formations arrive.

focuses.title: Fund Shelters, Sirens and Community Training
focuses.description: Open a supervised civil-protection grant round. Rescue services and councils must demonstrate how warning systems, shelter access and evacuation exercises will work together.

focuses.title: Back Joint Defence-Industry Development
focuses.description: Select inspected prototypes and supplier partnerships with domestic firms. Contracts should retain technical knowledge and service capacity in Estonia.

focuses.title: Finance an Ammunition Manufacturing Workshop
focuses.description: Purchase a limited production facility and qualify its suppliers. Its output still depends on workers, materials and ordinary production orders.

focuses.title: Finance Military Equipment Servicing Capacity
focuses.description: Fund an overhaul workshop and replacement-component tooling. This investment adds capacity for the equipment Estonia can actually afford to procure.

focuses.title: Launch the Regional Skilled-Jobs Investment Round
focuses.description: Negotiate assessed projects with councils, employers and worker representatives. Publish the training obligations and employment results attached to each award.

focuses.title: Fund Applied Research and Industrial Automation
focuses.description: Award competitive grants against credible delivery milestones. Researchers and manufacturers should share the practical risks of bringing a new process into production.

focuses.title: Tender the Unserved Broadband Connections
focuses.description: Target connections that commercial rollout has left behind. Contracts need service standards, realistic maintenance obligations and access for local firms and schools.

focuses.title: Finance Assessed Renewable-Power Projects
focuses.description: Contract viable generating capacity with clear delivery and reliability obligations. Investment must account for balancing needs and the networks serving each project.

focuses.title: Fund Thirty-Kilowatt Household Grid Connections
focuses.description: Finance the proposed connection allowance through transparent eligibility rules. Operators must assess network capacity before promising a household that it can export power.

focuses.title: Open the Inclusive Energy-Renovation Grant Round
focuses.description: Commission supervised building upgrades with accessible designs. The grant round targets high losses and practical savings instead of declaring the housing stock modernised at once.

focuses.title: Contract Strategic Energy Reserves and Storage
focuses.description: Budget tested reserves and storage trials for interrupted supply. Stock management and replacement schedules must be included in every contract.

focuses.title: Support Community Energy Cooperatives
focuses.description: Provide technical assistance and accountable finance for viable shared projects. Members receive clear contracts covering ownership, maintenance and their share of the risks.

focuses.title: Modernise District Heating with Reserve Capacity
focuses.description: Tender heat-network upgrades against verified demand. Councils must preserve a workable fallback while replacing inefficient equipment and pipes.

focuses.title: Legislate the Twenty-Eight-Percent Upper Tax Band
focuses.description: Publish the new income and dividend schedules with clear filing guidance. Additional receipts enter the public ledger alongside the administration costs.

focuses.title: Agree the Steps toward a Twelve-Hundred-Euro Minimum Wage
focuses.description: Negotiate funded stages with the social partners and inspect implementation. Transitional assistance helps smaller employers adapt without treating a statutory target as instant prosperity.

focuses.title: Extend Sectoral Collective Bargaining
focuses.description: Resource mediation and enforcement so agreements can operate beyond the strongest workplaces. Publish coverage and compliance data with unions and employers.

focuses.title: Fund Working-Time Study and Career Changes
focuses.description: Open assessed training places and agree study arrangements with employers. Public support follows completed learning and practical opportunities to change occupation.

focuses.title: Fund the Indexed Hundred-and-Fifty-Euro Child Benefit
focuses.description: Finance the proposed benefit level with delivery checks and a published review. Families need predictable support and a service that handles their claims reliably.

focuses.title: Commission the First Public Rental-Housing Tranche
focuses.description: Assess sites, construction costs and long-term management before awarding the first projects. Housing providers remain accountable for upkeep and access.

focuses.title: Finance Universal Health-Insurance Access
focuses.description: Update eligibility, service purchasing and public funding together. Coverage must be supported by commissioned care and a practical route for patients to use it.

focuses.title: Commission Community Mental-Health Services
focuses.description: Train and contract staff for accessible referrals, prioritising children and young people. Review waiting times and coordination with schools and primary care.

focuses.title: Fund a Step toward the Pension Objective
focuses.description: Authorize an affordable increase and publish the outstanding liability. Pension policy needs dependable financing rather than an unfunded declaration that the target has been met.

focuses.title: Make Assessed Residential Care Affordable on a Pension
focuses.description: Contract places against care-quality and staffing standards. Councils must explain assessed needs, fees and the public contribution to each family.

focuses.title: Fund the Teachers' Salary and Career Agreement
focuses.description: Negotiate salary stages, training places and manageable workloads with schools. Publish progress alongside vacancies and retention rather than promising staff who are not available.

focuses.title: Resource Shared Estonian-Language Schooling
focuses.description: Provide trained language staff, learning materials and specialist support. Schools need practical help to teach children from different home-language backgrounds together.

focuses.title: Present the Social Democratic Government's Accounts
focuses.description: Report funded reforms, readiness and outstanding commitments to parliament. The next mandate should begin with an honest account of what has been delivered.

focuses.title: An Eesti 200 Long-Term Parliamentary Mandate
focuses.description: The largest delegation must now turn a long-term programme into funded decisions. A confirmed majority will answer to parliament for education, resilient government and defence preparation.

focuses.title: Fund the Three-Percent Defence Commitment
focuses.description: Approve a procurement and operating tranche toward the proposed defence commitment. Delivery schedules and continuing costs go before parliament for review.

focuses.title: Prepare the Kalevipoja Air-Defence Dome
focuses.description: Survey sites and fund trained crews, communications and compatible purchases. The proposed integrated shield needs a staged procurement plan rather than a declaration that the sky is already secure.

focuses.title: Assign Every Citizen a Crisis Role
focuses.description: Test the reserve call-up lists and coordinate civilian responsibilities with employers and councils. Exercises must reveal which plans can actually assemble and sustain the existing units.

focuses.title: Fund Kaitseliit Instructors and Civil-Protection Training
focuses.description: Commission professional instruction for volunteers in military and civilian emergencies. Inspect equipment upkeep and realistic arrangements for participants with civilian jobs.

focuses.title: Prepare Sustained Allied Reception
focuses.description: Exercise ports, routes and dispersed stores with Estonia's available allies. Facilities support the reinforcement agreements that actually exist in this campaign.

focuses.title: Establish Civil Reserves and Tartu Disaster-Medicine Training
focuses.description: Finance community exercises and a first training tranche for military and disaster medicine in Tartu. Local services must demonstrate warning, shelter and evacuation arrangements together.

focuses.title: Capitalize Domestic Defence-Industry Projects
focuses.description: Award assessed development finance to domestic suppliers. The state acts as an inspected development partner while firms remain responsible for delivery and usable products.

focuses.title: Finance Domestic Ammunition Manufacturing
focuses.description: Purchase a limited production facility and qualify its suppliers. Manufacturing still needs workers, materials and ordinary production orders.

focuses.title: Equip a Defence Servicing and Components Workshop
focuses.description: Finance overhaul tooling and domestic component supply alongside the production programme. This is capacity for equipment Estonia can procure and maintain.

focuses.title: Commission Dual-Use Drone Development Trials
focuses.description: Fund inspected prototypes and flight trials with domestic firms and researchers. Successful trials build expertise; they do not instantly supply combat aircraft.

focuses.title: Introduce the Business Research Tax Incentive
focuses.description: Publish eligible research costs and audit rules for the proposed incentive. Its recurring revenue cost enters the public ledger alongside the industrial benefit.

focuses.title: Simplify Small Companies and Raise the VAT Threshold
focuses.description: Implement the proposed simpler company form and hundred-thousand-euro VAT-registration threshold. Revised filing guidance accompanies the recorded revenue cost.

focuses.title: Create the Six-Month Renewable-Permit Procedure
focuses.description: Resource coordinated planning and assessed generating projects toward the proposed shorter procedure. Speed requires capable reviewers, clear standards and reliable delivery obligations.

focuses.title: Release Unused Grid Reservations and Fund Connections
focuses.description: Apply deadlines to unused connection bookings and finance bottleneck upgrades. Operators must demonstrate which projects can connect safely to the network.

focuses.title: Expand the Residential Energy-Renovation Programme
focuses.description: Commission supervised upgrades against verified heat losses. Funding covers a defined tranche toward the proposed larger renovation effort.

focuses.title: Offer Assessed Guarantees for Storage and Microgrids
focuses.description: Share defined technology risks with private investors and energy communities. Contracts specify maintenance, balancing obligations and the limits of public liability.

focuses.title: Design the Offshore Grid and Interconnector Programme
focuses.description: Commission surveys, permits and technical agreements for stronger Baltic links. Design work advances the programme without pretending that every proposed cable is already built.

focuses.title: Legislate the Climate Framework and Procurement Criteria
focuses.description: Publish consistent environmental duties and measurable procurement standards. Firms need dependable rules and transparent assessments when planning investment.

focuses.title: Enact the Once-Only Data Submission Rule
focuses.description: Connect eligible registries and remove repeated requests for information the state already holds. Test access controls and continuity before moving services to the new process.

focuses.title: Complete Public-Sector Electronic Invoicing
focuses.description: Migrate procurement payments to compatible machine-readable invoices. Audited administrative savings receive an explicit public-ledger balance amount.

focuses.title: Rebuild Expenditure through the Zero-Based Budget Review
focuses.description: Require departments to justify existing spending and publish the decisions. Only the reviewed savings enter the ledger; a review does not abolish public services by itself.

focuses.title: Launch Personal Health Accounts and the Employer Allowance
focuses.description: Build the proposed personal health account and twelve-hundred-euro employer contribution allowance. Privacy controls and the recurring fiscal cost accompany the rollout.

focuses.title: Place Health and Care Coordinators in Primary Care
focuses.description: Commission coordinators and interoperable case records across health and social services. Patients receive a practical route through services instead of disconnected referrals.

focuses.title: Fund Prevention and First-Line Mental-Health Services
focuses.description: Finance assessed prevention programmes, school support and primary-care referrals. Service contracts include trained staff, access standards and regular outcome reviews.

focuses.title: Start the Additional Education Investment Programme
focuses.description: Authorize the first funded stage toward the proposed annual education increase. Teacher recruitment, specialist support and regional delivery receive a common implementation plan.

focuses.title: Fund Teacher Careers toward the Three-Thousand-Euro Objective
focuses.description: Negotiate salary stages, professional development and workload rules. Publish progress toward the proposed pay objective without treating every vacancy as already filled.

focuses.title: Finance the Shared Estonian-Language School Transition
focuses.description: Provide language staff, learning materials and school support, including the Ida-Viru school-turnaround programme. Regional plans must support children with different home languages.

focuses.title: Extend Compulsory Learning to Eighteen
focuses.description: Resource flexible study and workplace-learning routes for young people after basic school. The new obligation requires suitable places and practical support for completion.

focuses.title: Reform Six-Thousand-Euro Student Loans and Repayment
focuses.description: Fund the revised loan scheme with a longer repayment period and clear eligibility. Publish the guarantee liability and terms so students can plan full-time study.

focuses.title: Launch the Shared Estonian e-University Platform
focuses.description: Commission accessible digital courses across higher-education institutions. Academic quality and practical access matter as much as the platform that distributes them.

focuses.title: Present the Eesti 200 Government's Accounts
focuses.description: Report funded reforms, defence preparation and outstanding commitments to parliament. The next mandate should inherit a clear account of delivery and remaining work.

focuses.title: A Parempoolsed Mandate for a Capable State
focuses.description: The new majority must reconcile a smaller civilian state with stronger defence. Parliament will scrutinize the funding and consequences of each reform.

focuses.title: Fund the Three-Percent Defence Investment Agreement
focuses.description: Approve the opening procurement tranche of a cross-party defence agreement. Allied reception remains a separate funding commitment.

focuses.title: Train Air-Defence Crews and Procure Communications
focuses.description: Use the investment plan to prepare sites, train crews and purchase compatible communications. Delivering a functioning capability requires sustained procurement.

focuses.title: Open Defence Roles to More Skills
focuses.description: Revise service rules and exercise existing call-up plans. Civilian specialists, alternative service and voluntary service can fill genuine capability gaps.

focuses.title: Organize the Ten-Thousand-Person Civil Reserve
focuses.description: Begin registering and training a nonmilitary reserve toward the proposed ten-thousand-person objective. Skills and civilian availability must be verified.

focuses.title: Fund Allied Reception Outside the Defence Baseline
focuses.description: Prepare routes and dispersed stores with the allies available to Estonia. Reception funding supports the reinforcement agreements that actually exist.

focuses.title: Exercise Estonia's Essential Services in Isolation
focuses.description: Test dispersed stocks, emergency communications and private suppliers. Ministries must show how essential services would function while outside connections are interrupted.

focuses.title: Open Defence Suppliers' Access to Capital
focuses.description: Use competitive loan and equity finance for private suppliers. Procurement contracts specify deliverables, investment risk and the limits of public participation.

focuses.title: Contract a Domestic Ammunition Production Line
focuses.description: Finance tooling against an inspected supply contract with domestic industry. The production line still needs materials, workers and ordinary military orders.

focuses.title: Contract Military Servicing and Component Capacity
focuses.description: Purchase overhaul tooling and qualified component capacity from domestic suppliers. Contract inspections must demonstrate that the investment can maintain Estonia's equipment.

focuses.title: Sign the Three-Percent Research Agreement
focuses.description: Agree a staged public-private research programme with business organizations. Contracts define measurable innovation outcomes and the responsibilities of participating firms.

focuses.title: Tie University Funding to Knowledge Transfer
focuses.description: Commission joint university-industry development projects and publish their results. Funding rewards usable knowledge transfer rather than disconnected research and production plans.

focuses.title: Introduce the Skilled-Migration Points System
focuses.description: Create a transparent admission system for qualifications and labour-market needs. Language support and assessed security conditions accompany skilled-worker recruitment.

focuses.title: Clear Planning Barriers to Private Renewable Projects
focuses.description: Simplify spatial planning and resource permit review. Stable rules and competent decisions support private investment without introducing a new blanket generation subsidy.

focuses.title: Co-Finance Offshore-Wind Grid Connections
focuses.description: Prepare assessed connections and seek available European co-financing. Operators must demonstrate safe integration and credible delivery schedules for new capacity.

focuses.title: Keep Dispatchable Capacity Ready During the Transition
focuses.description: Fund maintenance and demand-management readiness while replacement capacity develops. Dependable existing generation remains available during the energy emergency.

focuses.title: Prepare Nuclear Licensing and Independent Oversight
focuses.description: Draft the rules and recruit supervisory expertise for possible private nuclear development. Licensing preparation creates no reactor or nuclear weapons.

focuses.title: Simplify Residential Energy Renovation
focuses.description: Coordinate renovation procedures and technical advice. Homeowners and qualified firms gain a clearer route to investments that reduce wasted heat.

focuses.title: Specify Timber for Public Construction
focuses.description: Qualify durable timber construction and transparent procurement criteria. Public contracts support higher-value materials while retaining safety and building-performance standards.

focuses.title: Audit the State's Activities and Duplicated Agencies
focuses.description: Publish service costs and review overlapping responsibilities. Ministers must identify actual savings and the services affected before presenting a revised budget.

focuses.title: Pass the Negative Supplementary Budget
focuses.description: Cancel reviewed low-priority spending and consolidate duplicated functions. The reduction improves the ledger but creates disputes over withdrawn public commitments.

focuses.title: Publish Understandable Budgets and Traceable Services
focuses.description: Make expenditure decisions and service progress visible to citizens. Departmental reporting must explain public costs and permit meaningful parliamentary scrutiny.

focuses.title: Stage the Eighteen-Percent Income Tax and Social-Tax Cap
focuses.description: Schedule lower income tax and a social-tax ceiling at three average wages. Record the revenue reduction alongside the expected competitiveness gain.

focuses.title: Exempt Employee Transport, Meals and Health Benefits
focuses.description: Remove fringe-benefit tax from specified employee costs. Publish eligibility and anti-abuse rules together with the recurring revenue reduction.

focuses.title: End Parliamentary Earmarks and Political Slush Funds
focuses.description: Replace discretionary political grants with transparent appropriations and stronger local oversight. Public money requires a defensible purpose and a visible recipient.

focuses.title: Direct Seventy Percent of Education Spending to Teachers
focuses.description: Rebalance school budgets toward teaching and give principals responsibility for rewarding performance. Training and modern learning platforms accompany the proposed pay reforms.

focuses.title: Support the Common Estonian-Language School
focuses.description: Fund language support and teaching materials for a shared school system. Integration must preserve teaching quality and help pupils participate in Estonian society.

focuses.title: Commission Vocational and Mid-Career Retraining
focuses.description: Expand assessed vocational places and competitive training contracts. Working adults need practical access to new skills while maintaining employment.

focuses.title: Pair University Contributions with Student Assistance
focuses.description: Introduce partial tuition with revised loans, grants and employer-paid study. Additional university resources come with public concern over affordability.

focuses.title: Replace Blanket Benefits with Needs-Based Assistance
focuses.description: Use safeguarded public records to direct support toward households in need. Reassessment saves expenditure but unsettles families losing universal entitlements.

focuses.title: Open Care Contracts and Reduce Medical Paperwork
focuses.description: Commission care competitively and expand electronic referrals with administrative support. Contracts must preserve access while clinicians spend more time treating patients.

focuses.title: Present the Parempoolsed Government's Accounts
focuses.description: Present defence deliveries, tax receipts and the costs of structural reform. Parliament must assess the remaining commitments before another mandate.
